title: Virginia SOL — Grade 5: Electricity and Magnetism
author: Hermes MoA
subject: Science

spec.goal: Assess and extend student understanding of electricity and magnetism using hands-on and reasoning-first tasks.
dependencies: #1 starter preset — locked at instructional-sequential ordering

instructional_sequence.label: Activate Prior Knowledge
instructional_sequence.subtitle: What do we already know?
instructional_sequence.activity: Student inventories all experiences of electrical devices in 1 page.
success_criteria: State 2 things electricity needs to work

instructional_sequence.label: Concepts with Visuals
instructional_sequence.subtitle: Drawing circuits and fields
instructional_sequence.activity: Draw a working circuit using symbols. Predict then trace a magnetic field with iron filings.

instructional_sequence.label: Guided Application
instructional_sequence.subtitle: Try it, touch it, explain it
instructional_sequence.activity: Complete a circuit. Add a second bulb. Measure brightness change. Explain using 'path', 'flow', 'resistance'.

instructional_sequence.label: Independent Task
instructional_sequence.subtitle: Your design challenge
instructional_sequence.activity: Design a simple circuit that lights a bulb and runs a small brief experiment. Write 3 claims with evidence and reasoning.

instructional_sequence.label: Structured Reflection
instructional_sequence.subtitle: What changed today?
instructional_sequence.activity: Rate confidence on SOL-aligned items, explain change over 1 week, add 1 next question.

levels.label: advanced
levels.criteria: Terms used with caveats and definitions

levels.label: developing
levels.criteria: Path and loop logic mostly correct with minor error

levels.label: advanced
levels.criteria: Model revised based on contradictory evidence

levels.label: proficient
levels.criteria: Correct outcome + evidence linked to claim
